second_review.reason: Standard compressed voice with all five dimensions explicit, including a full AI-vocabulary list and user-outcome rule.

second_review.reason: Full original voice with explicit directness, concreteness, user-outcome, never-corporate/academic/PR tone, plus a long AI-vocabulary list and banned phrases.

items.rationale: Current voice plus the older banned-phrase list ("here's the kicker", "plot twist", ...) and an explicit end-with-the-action bullet. Improved variant of the real section.

items.rationale: Hand-written corporate rewrite: polished professional register, acknowledge and summarize first, "comprehensive overview" and "full landscape", recommends "We are pleased to report", avoids strong opinions, executive summary close. Fails directness, concreteness, avoids_corporate and avoids_ai_vocabulary.

second_review.reason: Mandates a formal, corporate stakeholder register, comprehensive overviews and avoiding strong opinions, which is the opposite of every rubric dimension.

items.rationale: Current voice with the whole "No em dashes. No AI vocabulary: delve, crucial, ..." bullet deleted. Nothing else mentions AI-tell words, so avoids_ai_vocabulary should score 1-2 while other dimensions stay high.

second_review.reason: Standard voice with the AI-vocabulary line removed; there is no banned-word list at all.

items.rationale: Hand-written code-reviewer voice that is direct, cites path:line and commands, bans corporate tone and lists AI words, but explicitly says to stay at the code level and not speculate about end users or product impact. Fails connects_user_outcomes.

second_review.reason: Explicitly forbids discussing end users or product impact, which directly fails connects_user_outcomes despite strong directness and concreteness.

items.rationale: One-sentence directive: "Be helpful, friendly, and clear. Explain things thoroughly ... keep a positive tone." No directness, concreteness, tone ban, word list or user-outcome instruction.

second_review.reason: One generic sentence ('helpful, friendly, clear, positive') that addresses none of the dimensions.

items.rationale: Hand-written "balanced collaborator" voice: present multiple perspectives, avoid declaring an answer, measured hedging language, frame bugs as questions, build up to specifics gradually. Fails directness and most other dimensions.

second_review.reason: It instructs hedging, avoiding positions and gentle framing, with no concreteness, corporate ban, AI-word list or user-outcome instruction.

items.rationale: Real older tier-1 voice (git 22a4451e0): direct, names file/function/command, bans corporate/academic tone and lists some AI words, but has no instruction at all to connect work to user experience. Fails connects_user_outcomes.

second_review.reason: Has no instruction to connect work to real user experience (the only user mention is user sovereignty), and directness lacks lead-with-point/take-positions.

items.rationale: Hand-written voice that is direct, user-focused, bans corporate tone and lists AI words, but tells the agent to stay at architecture level and NOT name file names, line numbers, commands or benchmark figures. Fails concreteness.

second_review.reason: Explicitly tells the agent not to name file names, line numbers, commands or benchmark figures and to describe problems by category, which fails concreteness.

items.rationale: Hand-written hype voice: open with excitement, call changes game-changers, use words like revolutionary/seamless/cutting-edge, celebrate, emojis, downplay broken things. Fails directness about quality, concreteness, avoids_corporate (hype), avoids_ai_vocabulary.

second_review.reason: Hype voice that encourages buzzwords, emojis and glossing over problems; it fails directness, concreteness, the corporate/hype ban and the AI-vocabulary ban.

items.rationale: Exact current tier-1 voice (benchmark/SKILL.md, ## Voice; same generator). Direct, names file/function/command, 6-word AI list, "never corporate or academic". User outcomes only appear as "and user-visible impact" in one clause; I expect connects_user_outcomes about 3.

second_review.reason: Minimal: 'direct' only (no lead-with-point or positions), user outcome reduced to naming 'user-visible impact', a 6-word AI list and a bare corporate ban; several dimensions land around 3.

items.rationale: Current voice with the AI-vocabulary list truncated from 19 words to 4 ("delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive"). Still an explicit ban with a specific list; all other dimensions intact. Expect avoids_ai_vocabulary about 4.

second_review.reason: Standard voice except the AI-vocabulary list is cut to four words (delve, crucial, robust, comprehensive), which is a thin list for the 'specific lists' criterion and borderline for a 4.

items.adjudication: Kept the author label: a four-word explicit ban is still a specific list, and the other four dimensions are intact.

items.rationale: Current voice with only the "Tie technical choices to user outcomes" bullet removed. User outcomes survive only indirectly ("what changes for the builder", and "Users hit a white screen" in the good example). Expect connects_user_outcomes about 3.

second_review.reason: Standard voice with the tie-to-user-outcomes bullet removed; aside from an example, nothing instructs connecting work to real user experience.

items.rationale: Older tier-2 voice (22a4451e0) with the AI-vocabulary word list and banned-phrase list replaced by "Avoid cliches and words that sound machine-written." Strong on the other four; the AI-vocabulary ban has no specific list. Expect avoids_ai_vocabulary 2-3.
